title: SEBI Streamlines Checks, Targets High-Risk Players

faq.q: What is SEBI's new inspection framework?
faq.a: SEBI's new framework shifts from routine, broad-based inspections of market intermediaries to a targeted, risk-based approach. It aims to reduce overall inspection volume by two-thirds, focusing resources on entities identified as high-risk.

SEBI will likely use a combination of factors, including past compliance records, client complaint history, financial health, trading patterns, and other data analytics to identify intermediaries that pose a higher risk to the market or investors.

No, the goal is to enhance investor protection by making regulatory oversight more efficient and effective. By focusing on high-risk entities, SEBI can proactively address potential issues that could harm investors, rather than spreading resources thinly.

faq.q: How does this affect my stockbroker?
faq.a: If your stockbroker has a strong compliance record and good internal controls, they might face fewer routine inspections, potentially allowing them to focus more on service. If they have a history of issues, they will likely face more intense scrutiny.

faq.q: Where can I find information about SEBI's regulations?
faq.a: All official regulations, circulars, and notifications from SEBI are published on their official website, sebi.gov.in. This is the most reliable source for up-to-date information.
